claims.text: Enhanced corrosion resistance in stainless steels used for chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications arises from rapid self-healing of a Cr2O3-rich passive film.
A fine-grained microstructure with high grain-boundary density enables passive-film self-healing by promoting Cr diffusion from the bulk to the surface.
Grain-boundary-assisted Cr transport rapidly replenishes oxide lost or damaged at localized corrosion sites.
The baseline is a conventional stainless steel with standard Cr content and a relatively coarse-grained microstructure typical of chemical-processing and nuclear-power applications.
Controlled rolling and annealing can produce a fine-grained variant with increased grain-boundary area while retaining constant Cr content.
The controlled study will compare coarse- and fine-grained stainless steels while holding Cr content constant.
The relevant structural mediator is a continuous, thin, Cr-enriched passive film composed predominantly of Cr2O3.
Higher grain-boundary density enhances the formation and repair of the Cr-enriched passive film.
Refined grains accelerate Cr diffusion along grain boundaries.
Accelerated Cr transport permits efficient repair of a compromised passive oxide film.
Dynamic repassivation limits localized metal dissolution and retards corrosion under harsh thermal and chemical conditions.
Relative to the coarse-grained baseline, fine-grained steel will form a more uniform, stable, and Cr2O3-rich passive film.
Relative to the coarse-grained baseline, fine-grained steel will exhibit lower corrosion-current density and mass-loss rate.
Relative to the coarse-grained baseline, fine-grained steel will exhibit improved electrochemical-impedance characteristics.
The coarse-grained baseline develops its passive film more slowly and has a higher corrosion rate than the proposed fine-grained variant under otherwise identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism should operate at service temperatures and radiation levels typical of chemical-processing and nuclear environments when Cr content is sufficiently high.
The mechanism may become ineffective under extreme film disruption, reduced Cr content, or interference from detrimental secondary phases.
The cited study demonstrates that duplex stainless steel 2205 can be evaluated by potentiodynamic polarization and mass-loss measurements during elevated-temperature chloride-salt corrosion exposure.
The relative contributions of alloy chemistry and grain-boundary density to repassivation kinetics are not fully quantified.
The in-service effect of irradiation on grain-boundary diffusion is uncertain.
